verdict.rationale: Terraform's core product is a CLI whose source is published on GitHub, and it runs on the user's own machine. It keeps state locally or in a remote backend of the user's choosing, and the plan/apply workflow needs no vendor-hosted service, so the core is self-hostable by design. The evidence never states this outright, and community discussion flags the BUSL license's vague 'competitive offering' wording as a constraint on openness. missing for 10: explicit first-party self-hosting/installation docs, clarity on BUSL license terms for self-hosted use, evidence of self-hosted equivalents to HCP Terraform features (policy enforcement, workspaces)
